A compact description of a plan, for an agent's context

Source: R/describe.R
describe_plan.Rd

Summarises a MediaPlan as a plain named list an agent can read before it proposes an edit: what the plan is, how it is keyed, what it spends and on what, what cannot move, what it buys, when it spends, and the values an op may target. Every section is capped – the top_n values by spend, plus a count and total for the rest – so the description stays the same size whether the plan has fifty rows or fifty thousand.

Usage

describe_plan(
  plan,
  top_n = 10,
  budget = NULL,
  models = NULL,
  constraints = NULL,
  reference = NULL,
  as_json = FALSE
)

Arguments

plan

A MediaPlan.

top_n

How many values to list for each column before the rest are summarised. A whole number, 1 or more.

budget

Optional budget envelope, as check_budget() takes it. Adds a budget section.

models

Optional fitted response models, as model_map() takes them. Adds a models section.

constraints

Optional PlanConstraints. Adds a constraints section.

reference

The plan change rules in constraints are measured against; see check_constraints().

as_json

FALSE (default) returns the nested list; TRUE returns it as JSON text.

Value

A named list with the sections above, or a json string when as_json = TRUE. Lists that can hold several values (grain, edits, subplan_cells, top values) stay JSON arrays even with one element.

Details

Everything is derived from the plan on the call, and the numbers reconcile to @data: each column's breakdown, the commitments and the months all add up to the total. Money is rounded to the cent, shares to four places, and dates are ISO strings on the plan's clock, so the list serializes to JSON as it stands.

Sections

identity

name, nickname, id and parent_id (short ids), status, approved_on, objective, the rationale's author, and edits – the ops that derived it from its parent, in order ("allocation" for an allocation edit; empty for a root).

shape

grain (coarsest first, time last), time_col, time_basis, tz, the flight window, n_line_items, n_rows, is_topline and the subplan_cells a subplan owns.

money

spend_basis – what every figure measures ("" when undeclared) – total, and spend_by each line item column: its top values (value, spend, share) and an other bucket (n_values, spend).

commitments

Spend that cannot move, from the spend bounds (bound_cols()): committed (rows whose min and max equal their spend), floor_locked (the floors under rows with a floor), flexible (rows with no floor), headroom (all spend an edit could take out: the flexible spend plus what sits above floors), and n_bounded_line_items. A plan with no bounds is all headroom.

units

One row per unit type: planned_units, the planned_spend behind them, and the blended rate (a CPM for impressions).

time

Spend by calendar month, via calendarize().

targetable

What an op's target may name: for each line item column, its top values by spend and n_more; for the time column, the first and last value and how many there are. The full lists are in plan_ops_schema() for the plan.

budget

Only when budget is given: how the plan sits against it, from check_budget() at its default tolerance – n_rows, n_within, and the envelopes off it, worst first (envelope, amount, planned, variance, in_plan), capped at top_n with n_more_off for the rest.

models

Only when models is given: how much of the plan its response models cover, from model_map() – modeled_share, unmodeled_spend, n_models_used, and the largest unmodeled line items, capped at top_n with n_more_unmodeled for the rest.

constraints

Only when constraints is given: how the plan stands against them, from check_constraints() – the rule set's id, n_rules, n_ok, the violated rules (worst first) and the binding ones, which hold with no slack to spare, so the next edit that pushes on them breaks them. Each capped at top_n.

See also

plan_ops_schema() for the full contract an agent's ops are checked against; line_item_summary() for the uncapped roster.

Examples

plan <- media_plan_from_df(
  data.frame(month = rep(as.Date(c("2026-10-01", "2026-11-01")), each = 3),
             channel = c("Streaming", "Search", "Social"),
             planned_spend = c(60000, 20000, 10000, 40000, 20000, 10000),
             min_spend = c(60000, 15000, NA, 40000, 15000, NA),
             max_spend = c(60000, NA, NA, 40000, NA, NA)),
  grain = "channel", time = "month", name = "Q4"
)
d <- describe_plan(plan, top_n = 2)
d$money$spend_by$channel
#> $top
#>       value spend share
#> 1 Streaming 1e+05 0.625
#> 2    Search 4e+04 0.250
#> 
#> $other
#> $other$n_values
#> [1] 1
#> 
#> $other$spend
#> [1] 20000
#> 
#> 
d$commitments
#> $committed
#> [1] 1e+05
#> 
#> $floor_locked
#> [1] 30000
#> 
#> $flexible
#> [1] 20000
#> 
#> $headroom
#> [1] 30000
#> 
#> $n_bounded_line_items
#> [1] 2
#> 

cat(describe_plan(plan, as_json = TRUE))
